channels.name: Word Of Mouth
channels.blurb: Spend nothing. Let it find who it finds.
channels.body: No campaign, no banner, no influencer package. Either the thing is good enough that people tell each other, or it is not. There is a purity to this and it is frequently very expensive.

channels.name: Trailer Campaign
channels.blurb: Reliable, unglamorous, works exactly as well as you pay for.
channels.body: Ninety seconds cut by people who cut ninety seconds for a living, placed in front of things people were already watching. No upside surprise, no downside surprise, and the graph moves.

channels.name: Influencer Package

risk.name: The Disclosure
risk.line: One of them forgot the #ad tag and a very thorough person found the contract. It is a thread now.

channels.blurb: Biggest reach per dollar. Somebody will forget to disclose.
channels.body: Forty creators, one embargo, an agency in the middle taking a cut everyone pretends not to see. The numbers are undeniable and the whole apparatus is one screenshot away from being the story.

channels.name: Awards Push
channels.blurb: Screeners, juries, a table at the ceremony. Standing and score, not copies.
channels.body: You are not buying sales, you are buying a sentence in a press release and a photograph of you clapping. It is the purest form of industry money there is and it works every single time.

channels.name: Seed The Discourse

risk.name: The Agency Invoice
risk.line: An invoice from the agency leaked with two hundred account handles on it. Every one of them had defended you by name.

channels.blurb: Manufactured argument. Enormous reach. Roughly a one-in-three chance of being caught.
channels.body: Nobody in this room will use the word astroturf. The deck says 'organic-adjacent seeding.' It moves the wishlist graph like nothing else on this list and the invoice exists, somewhere, in someone's inbox.

channels.name: Just Show The Game
channels.blurb: Raw footage, no target render, no cinematic. Trust climbs hard.
channels.body: It looks worse than the competition and it is the only honest thing on the storefront. Fewer people see it. The ones who do arrive already on your side, and they stay for the next three titles.

channels.name: Festival Circuit
channels.blurb: Showcases, demos, a queue of strangers. Slow, cheap, genuinely effective.
channels.body: Four events, a folding table, and eleven hundred people who played it with you standing behind them. Half the coverage you get for the next year traces back to somebody's twenty minutes in that queue.

backlash.name: Refund Wave
backlash.line: The refund window becomes a news story. Thirty percent of week one walks back out through the door it came in.

backlash.name: Quietly Delisted
backlash.line: One storefront removes it without an announcement. Support tickets are answered with a link to a policy page.

backlash.name: Advertisers Walk
backlash.line: Three sponsors exit the campaign mid-flight. The bookings were non-refundable. Yours were.

backlash.name: Review Bomb
backlash.line: Eleven thousand one-star reviews in four hours, most of them from accounts with no playtime and a great deal of energy.

backlash.name: The Open Letter
backlash.line: Forty industry figures sign a letter about you. Nine of them have taken your money. All nine mention courage.

backlash.name: A Regulator Opens A File
backlash.line: A jurisdiction you had not thought about has thoughts about your surprise mechanics. The fine is survivable. The precedent is not.

backlash.name: It Backfired Upward
backlash.line: The attempt to bury it put it on the front page of four sites at once. Wishlists tripled overnight. Nobody involved intended this.

backlash.name: The Clip
backlash.line: Nine seconds of your worst bug became the funniest thing on the internet for a day. Sales did a thing the model did not predict.
